A Life Remembered

His Story

Edward Kwaku Antwi Kajah was born on 5th January 1966 at Agona Mankrong in the Central Region, the youngest of seven children of Mr. John Kwaku Saah Kajah and Madam Kate Akua Kakraba Ntsiful, both of blessed memory. He began his education at Mankrong L/A School and continued at Akim Oda L/A School, before moving to Tema Community 5 in the early 1980s to live with his aunt, the late Christiana Esi Bortey.

He ventured into the gas cylinder trade, first in Kumasi and later at Tema Community 1, where — with the support of his elder brother Joe and Mr. Reginald Kofi Paitoo — he built the shop that would define much of his working life. It was during this season that he married and was blessed with three children.

Illness later drew him back into his brother Joe's care, and after Joe's sudden passing in December 2020, Edward continued treatment and recovery at Oda Abenase under the devoted care of his uncle Papa Koranteng and sister Adwoa. In October 2025, after years apart, he finally returned to Tema to reunite with his children — a homecoming that lasted just seven months before his passing on 21st May 2026 at 37 Military Hospital, following a sudden collapse on the evening of 19th May.

A faithful worshipper of the Methodist Church, Edward is remembered as a devoted father, a steadfast brother, and — to his late brother Joe's children — the "Wofa Kwaku" who stepped in without hesitation whenever he was needed, carrying burdens that were never officially his to carry.

"Me ma mo nnansa pɛ." — "I give you only three days." A running joke Edward left behind, still spoken with love
